chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated that Abu Ya'la al-Mooseli narrated that Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shoyba narrated from Hatam ibn Isma'il, from Al-Muhajir ibn Mismar, from Al-Amir ibn Sa'd, who said: I wrote to Jabir ibn Samurah with my servant Nafi', asking him to inform me of something he had heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He wrote: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say on a Friday evening, on the day Al-Aslami was stoned: 'The religion will remain firm until the Hour comes, and there will be twelve Caliphs over you, all of them from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number of Caliphs after him?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Jabir ibn Samurah establishes the twelve Caliphs as a definitive sign of Islam's continuity until the Day of Resurrection, specifying their lineage from Quraysh. In Shia scholarship, this is a primary proof text for the Imamate of the Twelve Imams, linking the political and spiritual succession directly to the Prophet’s explicit designation. The mention of 'evening' (ashiya) during the Friday sermon highlights the public and urgent nature of this announcement.
